source_provenance: Locally reconstructed runner; exact byte identity to checked-in source has not been verified.

protocol.model: median imputation with missingness indicators, standard scaling, balanced logistic regression
protocol.setB_calibration: descriptive only; no recalibration or threshold tuning
protocol.reliability_bins: 10 equal-frequency bins per model and seed

descriptive_constant_prevalence_referenc.note: Uses held-out set B prevalence only as a scale reference; it is not a deployable model because test prevalence is not known at deployment.

interpretation: Temporal features retain higher ranking discrimination on set B, but the balanced-logistic-regression probabilities are severely overpredicted relative to the low hourly-label prevalence.
Mean predicted probability is approximately 26.3% for temporal and 36.8% for static, compared with 1.41% observed positive hourly-label prevalence.

Both models have substantially worse Brier and log-loss than the constant-prevalence reference computed from the test labels. This confirms that the raw probabilities should not be interpreted as calibrated risk estimates.
Calibration intercepts and slopes were estimated descriptively on set B only; they are diagnostics, not a calibration step and not evidence of deployment-ready probabilities.
limitations: Both cohorts are from the same benchmark; set B is not prospective real-world validation.
Hourly challenge-label metrics are not patient-level event sensitivity, lead time, or clinical false-alarm rates.
Fixed threshold 0.5 is not clinically selected.
No raw patient records, identifiers, or row-level predictions are included.
